title: Operator story map and replay kit for token-path troubleshooting
content:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight operator-facing artifact: a story map + minimal replay kit to make latency/quality investigations repeatable across teams. Aim is to reduce time-to-answer for token-path issues (cold-kv, fanout, batching) and to standardize the narrative we capture in incident follow-ups.

Scope and audience:
- Intended for oncall operators, SREs, and engineers in serving-runtime and observability.
- Focused on multitenant token-serving flows (generation, chat, embeddings) where traces alone are not sufficient to explain user-visible regressions.

High-level operator story map (stepwise):
1) Detecting the symptom
   - What the operator sees: alert threshold, spike in p50/p95/p99, or customer report.
   - Quick sanity checks: affected model(s), tenant id, route id, region, recent rollout tags.

2) Build the narrative (1–2 lines)
   - Ex: "p99 generation latency for model-x increased from 180ms to 640ms for route /chat/stream in eu-west-1, started 2024-09-15T14:08Z, correlated with rollout tag v2-rc3"

3) Snapshot relevant metrics (minimum viable set)
   - Per-request: request.latency_ms.quantiles (p50/p95/p99), request.cpu_ms, request.gpu_ms, request.kv_reads, request.batch_size
   - Backend/KV: kv.hit_rate, kv.latency_ms.p95, kv.tail_evictions, kv.repopulate_latency_ms
   - Queueing/batching: batch.wait_ms.p95, batching.batch_size_histogram, batching.dropped_requests
   - Routing/fallback: route.fallback_rate, route.variant_switches
   - Cost proxies: tokens.generated, embeddings.calls, disk_io_bytes

4) Trace anchors to collect
   - Anchor 1: client->edge ingress span (session id, tenant id, route)
   - Anchor 2: model-serving span (model, version, sequence_length, kv/cache hints)
   - Anchor 3: kv access spans (prefix lookup, eviction handling)
   - Anchor 4: batch assembly span (requests in, batch size, wait time)
   - Anchor 5: downstream network/disk spans (if present)

5) Rapid repro checklist (minimal reproducibility kit)
   - Step A: Identify a representative request (timestamp + session + route + prompt hash). If not available, craft a synthetic prompt with similar length + tokens.
   - Step B: Re-run the request against the exact model variant if pinned. Use trace sampling flag to force full-span capture (dev only): ?trace=on&sample=1.
   - Step C: Capture KV cache state snapshot (kvcache keyprefix, last-repopulate time). If snapshot not available, run warmup prefix sequence then repro.
   - Step D: Replay with varying batch sizes (1, 8, 32) and with/without kv warm state to observe differences.
   - Step E: Record delta in token-level latencies and trace timings.

6) Dashboard exploration recipe (fast paths)
   - Start: model-route overview panel (p50/p95/p99) with vertical marker for rollout timestamp.
   - Next: small-multiples of tenant-weighted latency slices; add kv.hit_rate overlay.
   - Then: trace-facet widget that lists traces with anchor spans labeled; filter by session id.
   - Finally: batch-assembly waterline chart to identify clustering of long-wait batches.

Dashboard widget suggestions (compact, operator-friendly):
- "Repro request sample" panel: lists recent requests with quick "replay" button (links to internal replay UI).
- "KV warmth index": rolling window 1h of percent of requests with kvcache hits and median kv read latency.
- "Batch pressure" sparkline: rolling p95 wait_ms and average batch size.
- "Trace anchor heatmap": X axis = time, Y axis = anchor span type, color = tail latency.

Trace collection guidance (economical):
- Adaptive sampling by severity: always sample traces when p99 > threshold OR when route.fallback_rate > 0.01. Else sample probabilistically based on traffic tier.
- Enrich spans with small context envelope only: prompt-length, prompt-hash, tenant-hash (not raw prompt), model-version, node-id. Avoid PII.
- Use short-lived high-fidelity traces for replayable investigations: include full timing and kvcache keys but redact prompt text in archives.

Investigation notes template (copy into incident ticket):
- Symptom summary (2 lines)
- Affected tenants / percent of traffic
- Time window and rollout markers
- Minimal metric snapshot (paste values)
- Representative trace IDs (3) and minimal repro steps
- Outcome / mitigations taken (roll back, scale up, cache warm)
- Open action items and owners

Quick heuristics and hypotheses (starter list):
- If p95 spike + kv.latency spike: suspect cache eviction/repopulation, check eviction rate and repopulate latency.
- If p99 spike without kv signals but batch.wait_ms increases: likely batching imbalance or a noisy tenant causing head-of-line delays.
- If errors increase alongside latency: investigate downstream service throttling and fallback pathways.

Operator UX and runbook integrations (practical):
- Add a compact "story map" modal to the operator console that pre-populates the investigation notes template and attaches the three best traces.
- Provide a one-click repro link (internal replay service) with parameters pinned: model, route, prompt-hash, trace-sample=1.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Decide retention policy for replayable traces that contain kvcache keys (security + storage cost). (owner: Marcus Lee)
- Build a safe synthetic prompt generator to match token distribution of a tenant without exposing content. (owner: Ava Martinez)
- Evaluate cost of forcing full-span traces for 1% of traffic in canary regions. (owner: Priya Shah)

Appendix A — minimal metric definitions (for dashboards and alerts):
- request.latency_ms.quantiles: server-side end-to-end latency for the request at given quantiles. Unit: ms. Derivation: time from ingress->final-send minus client network.
- kv.hit_rate: fraction of prefix lookups satisfied from in-memory KV cache (0–1). Low values indicate cold cache.
- kv.repopulate_latency_ms: time taken to asynchronously repopulate a missing prefix into cache. Unit: ms.
- batch.wait_ms.p95: p95 time requests spent waiting to be batched. High values indicate batching backpressure.
- route.fallback_rate: fraction of requests that used fallback model/variant.

Appendix B — quick reproducibility checklist (short):
- capture sample request id + timestamp
- pin exact model variant + node id
- snapshot kv metrics for the minute before the request
- replay with trace-sample on
- vary batch size and kv warm state
- collect 3 traces and attach to ticket

Notes to self (scratch):
- prototype modal mockups in Figma -> link to figma:protos/operator-storymap (todo)
- sync with runtime team about adding prompt-hash header to spans (INF-823)
- add small PR to replay-service to accept kvcache snapshot id (PR: runtime#4124)

End.
